newsitem.title: USA: US House panel approves $209 mln FY98 SPR oil sale.
newsitem.headline: US House panel approves $209 mln FY98 SPR oil sale.

text.p: The U.S. House interior appropriations subcommittee on Tuesday approved a $13 billion fiscal 1998 spending bill that included a $209 million oil sale from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
The oil sale was needed to raise revenue to cover the cost of running the U.S. oil reserve.
The spending bill included no money to buy oil for the SPR in the 1998 fiscal year, which begins October 1, 1997.
The bill also included language saying that the committee expected 1998 to be the final year of oil sales to pay for operating the SPR.
In the last two years Congress has authorized the sale of about 30 million barrels from the SPR, first to pay for shutting down a damaged cavern in the reserve and then to help balance the budget.
The oil sales sparked strong opposition from leaders of the House Commerce Committee who say that the SPR should not be depleted just to generate cash.
The Clinton administration had proposed the sale of $1.15 billion worth of SPR oil in 2002 to help balance the budget but recently said such a sale would not be necessary.
